title: One coding fleet cut tokens per line by about 3.3 times
friendlyTitle: One person cut the tokens per line of code by about two thirds
summary: Alexander Marquardt measured ten weeks of Claude Code transcripts from a fleet he runs. Tokens per changed line fell about 3.3 times after he ended each agent at one task, kept the prompt cache warm, and loaded less into every session. He says several changes landed together, so he cannot separate every effect, and rework per pull request rose slightly.
friendlySummary: Alexander Marquardt counted ten weeks of transcripts from his own coding agents. After he gave each agent one task and stopped long idle sessions, tokens per changed line fell about 3.3 times. He says he cannot separate every change, and some rework went up.
whyItMatters: The bill is mostly context sent again on every call, not the code the agent writes. The first lever he would copy is measurement from the transcripts already on disk, then one task per session. The numbers are one project. They are not a benchmark.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Most of the cost is the old conversation sent again, not the new code. Start a fresh session for the next task, and measure what you already have on disk. These numbers are from one project.
